description: Cafofis is a multidisciplinary team combining Biology, Advertising, Marketing, and digital storytelling. LAST SIGNAL was initially developed by a Biology undergraduate, with an Advertising and Marketing student from ESAMC Uberlândia later joining the team to support communication and outreach. Our goal is to make NASA's scientific legacy accessible, engaging, and inspiring to future generations of explorers.
summary:
LAST SIGNAL is an interactive digital storytelling project designed to introduce young audiences to the legacy of NASA's retired space explorers.
 Through a mission-inspired virtual museum, visitors will explore the stories of Opportunity and Ingenuity, discovering their original objectives, scientific achievements, and the circumstances that ended their missions.
 Using authentic NASA mission resources, interactive storytelling, and accessible scientific explanations, the experience aims to transform complex exploration history into an engaging educational journey.
 Rather than presenting retired spacecraft as forgotten machines, LAST SIGNAL highlights how their discoveries continue to influence scientific knowledge and inspire future exploration.
 The project combines science communication, digital design, and educational storytelling to make space exploration more accessible to the next generation.
details:
LAST SIGNAL - The Museum of Silent Explorers

What if a space mission doesn't truly end when its spacecraft stops working?

This question is what inspired me to create LAST SIGNAL. We often think of space missions as journeys with a beginning and an end. A spacecraft is launched, it explores, makes discoveries, and eventually sends its final transmission. But I've come to believe that the end of a machine is not necessarily the end of its mission.

Opportunity spent nearly 15 years exploring Mars, despite being designed for a mission of just 90 Martian days. Ingenuity was expected to complete only five experimental flights, but went on to accomplish 72. Their instruments may have fallen silent, yet the knowledge they left behind continues to influence science, technology, and the way we imagine the future of exploration.

What fascinates me most is that scientific discoveries don't belong only to the moment in which they were made. Data collected years or even decades ago can still be revisited using new technologies, different methods, and questions that scientists had not yet thought to ask. Something discovered in the past can help us understand the present and inspire what we will build tomorrow.

I believe this is what makes exploration so meaningful. Its impact can extend far beyond the lifetime of the machines themselves. As long as there are people willing to learn, question, imagine, and build upon what came before them, the legacy of these missions continues.

With LAST SIGNAL, I wanted to create more than a digital museum about retired spacecraft. I wanted to create an experience that makes people feel connected to those discoveries. Something that encourages visitors, especially younger generations, to be curious, creative, and unafraid to imagine possibilities that may seem impossible today.

The interactive museum uses authentic NASA mission imagery and historical resources to tell the stories of Opportunity and Ingenuity. Visitors follow three stages: RECEIVE, where they encounter the missions and their records; DECODE, where they explore scientific discoveries through interactive questions and explanations; and TRANSMIT, where they reflect on what they have learned, consider a question for future exploration, and create their own digital transmission card.

That final stage is particularly important to me. I don't want visitors to simply look back at what others accomplished. I want them to recognize that they, too, can become part of what happens next. Maybe a photograph from Mars will inspire someone to study science. Maybe an old discovery will lead to a new idea. Maybe a question asked today will help shape a mission that hasn't even been imagined yet.

I developed LAST SIGNAL as a responsive website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with AI assistance for research organization, writing, design planning, and programming. The prototype is publicly hosted on Netlify and combines scientific information, visual storytelling, and interactive educational activities.

LAST SIGNAL was initially conceived and developed by me. Mariana, an Advertising and Marketing undergraduate student at ESAMC Uberlândia, later joined Cafofis, bringing a complementary perspective in communication, creativity, and audience engagement.

As a Biology undergraduate with an interest in scientific research and creative communication, this project also represents something personal: my belief that science should not only provide answers, but inspire people to keep asking questions.

I know this experience won't change the future of space exploration on its own. But I hope it might spark curiosity in someone who will.

Because perhaps the last signal of a mission is not the final message received on Earth. Perhaps it continues to echo through every discovery we revisit, every idea we develop, and every person inspired to explore something new.

The machines may have stopped transmitting. But humanity is still receiving, learning, and carrying their discoveries forward.

The last signal is ours to send!
